Robot Framework has native control structures, each closed with `END`:

- **`IF` / `ELSE IF` / `ELSE`** — branch on a condition. A one-line form,
  `IF    ${x} > 0    Log    positive`, handles simple cases.
- **`FOR`** — loop over a range or a collection: `IN`, `IN RANGE`,
  `IN ENUMERATE`, and `IN ZIP`.

`IN RANGE    1    5` counts 1, 2, 3, 4 — the end is exclusive, like Python.

## Task 1 — Write a FOR loop with an IF branch

**Goal:** in `checks/flow.robot`, count how many numbers in a range clear a
threshold, using a `FOR` loop with an `IF` branch inside.

Here is the same pattern over different data — counting how many temperature
readings are above freezing. Adapt the loop and condition to your numbers.

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Test Cases ***
Count Warm Readings
    ${warm}=    Set Variable    ${0}
    FOR    ${temp}    IN    -3    5    12    -1
        IF    ${temp} > 0
            ${warm}=    Evaluate    ${warm} + 1
        END
    END
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${warm}    2
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** `checks/flow.robot` uses a `FOR` loop and an `IF` branch, and the
count comes out right.

<!-- hint -->
Loop the numbers 1–4 with `FOR    ${n}    IN RANGE    1    5` (the end is
exclusive), starting a counter at `${0}` before the loop.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
Inside the loop, `IF    ${n} > 2` increment the counter with
`Evaluate    ${count} + 1`, and close both blocks with `END`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
Two numbers (3 and 4) clear the threshold, so assert the count is 2.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Test Cases ***
For And If
    ${count}=    Set Variable    ${0}
    FOR    ${n}    IN RANGE    1    5
        IF    ${n} > 2
            ${count}=    Evaluate    ${count} + 1
        END
    END
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${count}    2
```
<!-- /solution -->
